$comment: App-declared environment variables. Declare every variable this app reads beyond the platform-owned set; the Terp Studio deploy pipeline renders exactly the declared keys into a per-environment .app.env (see docker-compose.prod.yml), and `cp .app.env.example .app.env` exercises the same seam locally. Names match ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$. Mark write-only secrets with "format": "secret" — their values are sealed, never stored in plain records. A field this dialect does not have is REFUSED, because the deploy side drops what it does not recognise: "secret": true is the plausible mistake and it is not the field — it is dropped, and the value is then stored in plain records rather than sealed. format is one of secret | port | hostname | plain. requiredIn names where a value must be set: a non-empty list of ENVIRONMENT values (local | staging | production). "required" means every environment, so a name is in one or the other, never both; a value only a deployment needs — JOB_SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID is the canonical case, and a mail relay's MAIL_FROM and SMTP_HOST another (`terp guide mail`) — is declared "requiredIn": ["production"]. A variable whose last word is SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD, PASSPHRASE, KEY, CREDENTIAL or CREDENTIALS must declare one: "format": "secret" to seal it, or "format": "plain" to record that it holds no credential. Platform-owned names (SECRET_KEY, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, DATABASE_URL, ENVIRONMENT, WEB_PORT, BACKEND_CORS_ORIGINS) are refused here. LIMITS, and the reader fails closed on the WHOLE file past any of them: at most 50 variables; type/title/description/format/group/resolvedBy are strings of at most 500 characters each; enum is at most 50 strings of at most 200 characters. Keep a description to a sentence or two — an explanation long enough to be complete is easily past the cap, and it would cost the app every declaration in this file. A declared variable must NOT also appear in a compose `environment:` block: compose resolves `environment:` over `env_file:`, so the declaration would be dead — `terp verify --only env-seams` fails on that overlap. For an address, set "resolvedBy" to who resolves it, because it cannot be inferred from the name or type: "container" (a service on the compose network dials it — use the service name, http://api:8000), "host" (your shell dials it — http://127.0.0.1:8000), or "browser" (the user's browser is sent there — a host address). See `terp guide environment`.

MAIL_FROM.title: Sender
MAIL_FROM.description: The From of every mail the app sends: an address, or Name <address>. Production refuses to boot without a relay.

SMTP_HOST.title: Relay host
SMTP_HOST.description: The relay's bare hostname. The development stack runs a mail catcher under the name mailcatcher.

SMTP_PORT.title: Relay port
SMTP_PORT.description: Leave empty for the conventional port of the security mode: 587 for starttls, 465 for tls. The catcher listens on 1025.

SMTP_SECURITY.title: Relay security
SMTP_SECURITY.description: How the session to the relay is protected. none is for the development catcher only: a production boot refuses it.

SMTP_USERNAME.title: Relay account
SMTP_USERNAME.description: Set together with SMTP_PASSWORD, or neither. Never sent over an unencrypted session.

SMTP_PASSWORD.title: Relay password
SMTP_PASSWORD.description: Set together with SMTP_USERNAME, or neither.

SMTP_CA_FILE.title: Relay authority
SMTP_CA_FILE.description: Absolute path of a PEM file of the CA the relay's certificate must chain to, in place of the system's store: how a test environment trusts the TLS mail catcher it is given. Empty in development.

JOB_SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID.title: System actor
JOB_SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID.description: The id of the service principal a scheduled or user-less job's writes are stamped with. Production refuses to boot without it; development warns.
